subject: Thomas Brooks Park Archeological Dig Planning
overview: The commission found 69 Jerome Street significant, accepted four new demolition applications, and planned for an upcoming archeological dig at Thomas Brooks Park.

items.title: Significance Hearing: 69 Jerome Street
items.summary: Significance was found for the property due to its association with architect and builder Moses Mann.

items.title: Demolition Applications: 52 Alston, 146 Summer, and 232 Fulton Streets
items.summary: Accepted demolition applications for 52 Alston Street, 146 Summer Street, and 232 Fulton Street, with significance hearings scheduled for the following month.

items.title: Demolition Application: 130 Boston Avenue
items.summary: Accepted the application for demolition despite concerns regarding the accuracy of the architectural drawings and the current condition of the building.

items.title: Historical Survey Funding
items.summary: Approved $1,500 for survey documentation for three properties and an additional $500 for documentation of the Art Deco building at 4068 Mystic Valley Parkway.

items.title: Site Plan Review: 4060 Mystic Valley Parkway
items.summary: Determined that the submitted architectural drawings were too diagrammatic for the commission to provide formal comments to the city.

items.title: Community Preservation Committee Funding Discussion
items.summary: Discussed potential preservation projects for future grant cycles, including restoration of church steeples and private residential preservation incentives.

items.title: Thomas Brooks Park Archeological Dig
items.summary: Scheduled an archeological dig for May 2022 and planned a volunteer lottery for residents interested in participating.

items.title: Local Historic Districts Discussion
items.summary: Discussed the challenges of establishing local historic districts and the possibility of a single-building district for 78 Codding Street.
